text:
sam: Quick sync — I'm putting up a small proposal to change how we handle admission when a GPU pool hits saturation. current behavior is hard-reject at max_concurrency which is causing big error spikes for a few customer routes. thinking about a 'slowpath + opportunistic drop' model.

nina: +1 to rethinking. can you sketch the slowpath?

sam: idea = when pool_util > 0.95 we stop hard rejects and start sending non-critical requests to a degraded slowpath (longer queue, sloa=1000ms) and probabilistically drop after N retries. critical traffic (tier=A) still preferred. We also want zone-aware deprioritization so regions at capacity degrade first.

raj: curious about cost impact — longer queues == more GPU reservation time. have you run a sim?

sam: did a quick sim locally against last month's traffic dump. results: 1) p95 latency increases ~120ms for degraded requests 2) 40% fewer 5xx spikes vs hard-reject 3) extra GPU time ~6% under peak windows. tradeoff seems reasonable.

kai: can you share the sim config / snippet?

sam: pasted below:

```yaml
admission_policy:
  mode: hybrid_slowpath
  pool_threshold: 0.95
  slowpath:
    max_queue_ms: 1000
    max_attempts: 2
    drop_after_ms: 2000
  priority_map:
    A: always
    B: degrade_first
    C: degrade_first
  region_fallback: true
```

nina: nice. what about fairness? if a big customer keeps opening long-lived streams we could starve small requests on slowpath.

sam: slowpath will also include a short token-bucket per-customer limiter and aging: requests older than 800ms get lower weight. aim is short-term fairness.

ops-bot: NOTE: running canary on us-east-1/dev tomorrow 03:00 UTC. will auto-rollback on >1% customer 5xx increase or >10% p99 latency regression for tier A.

raj: canary thresholds seem tight but safe. does routing fallback to another region when slowpath engages? network egress cost could skyrocket.

sam: yes — region_fallback=true means if a replica in same region can't satisfy SLO we try next-preferred region. We'll tag fallbacks in traces and bill back cost center. ops-bot will capture counts.

kai: how will clients observe degrade vs reject? we should surface a clear error vs a header for degraded responses.

sam: plan: rejected requests return 429. degraded responses return 200 + header `X-Redwood-Degraded: true` and a small synthetic "latency_hint_ms" field in JSON. Also add a metrics label degraded=true.

grace: what about streaming? KV cache impact? if we move streaming calls to slowpath, KV warmups could spike.

sam: good call. streaming heavyweight calls are still on hard-priority (tier A) unless explicitly flagged degradable. We will add a config flag `streaming_degradable: false` by default.

nina: rollout plan?

sam: propose steps:
1) feature flag with default off; unit tests + e2e sim;
2) canary in us-east-1/dev (ops-bot scheduled);
3) short canary for small subset of prod routes (5%) for 2 hours; check metrics and traces;
4) expand to 25% with limits on region_fallback;
5) full rollout if no regressions.

raj: add a cost dashboard for region_fallback counts and incremental GPU-hours. ops-bot: can you wire a Grafana panel?

ops-bot: created dashboard link: https://grafana.redwood.local/d/AdmitHybrid/admit-hybrid-panel (private)

kai: ok i'm +1 pending sim reproducibility and a playbook for rollback. also add a customer communication plan if we see increased tail latency.

sam: will add rollback playbook (immediate revert flag + autoscaling bump) and docs for SEs. I'll open a follow-up PR w/ config, tests, and canary job.

nina: thanks — can you drop the sim artifacts in the thread? helps audits.

sam: done, sim tarball uploaded to s3: s3://redwood-infra/sims/admit-hybrid/2004005678-sim.tar.gz

grace: small ask — include a debug header when we fallback regions: `X-Redwood-Fallback: us-east-1->us-west-2` so tracing shows path.

sam: added to TODO.

ops-bot: Reminder: tagging this thread with #oncall and pinging ops on rollout. :bell:
